issues.failure_explanation: Since |alpha_3| <= sqrt(1-alpha_1^2), alpha_3(s) = -1 requires alpha_1(s) = 0, i.e. {2ts} = 1/2, where theta_1(alpha_1(s)) = theta_1(0) and floor(2ts) ranges over all of {0,...,2t-1}. The correct requirement is therefore theta_1(0) not congruent to -pi/2 - pi*k/t (mod 2pi) for all such k. The stated condition instead excludes theta_1(0) in {m*pi - 2n*pi/t} = gcd(t,2)*(pi/t)Z, which never equals the required set: e.g. for t = 1 the value theta_1(0) = -pi/2 is allowed but gives alpha_3(1/4) = sin(-pi/2) = -1 (likewise theta_1(0) = pi/2 for t = 2), so the factor sqrt(1+alpha_3(r)) in (eq:explicitweight3) vanishes and the formula does not define a map to S^3. The observation is false as stated.

Images of a weighted 1-design curve (left) and a weighted 3-design curve (right) on $S^3\cong\Bbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$ respectively resulting from the construction of Theorem \ref{thm:weightconst} applied to a 1-design set (antipodal points) and 3-design set (the vertices of an octahedron) on $S^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's final equality asserts that the normalized measure on S^d disintegrates along the height omega_1 as (1/2)ds times the normalized fiber measure. That is the height marginal only for d = 2 (Archimedes); for d >= 3 it is (omega_{d-1}/omega_d)(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}ds, not (1/2)ds. The pole-to-pole sweep makes w_R uniformly distributed on [-1,1] (as the proof's substitution factor lambda(x_i)/2 shows), so the identity fails for d >= 3 once t >= 2: for f(omega) = omega_1^2 the chain gives (1/2)int_{-1}^1 s^2 ds = 1/3, while int_{S^d} omega_1^2 d sigma = 1/(d+1), which differs for d >= 3. Hence for d >= 3, t >= 2 the constructed w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve; e.g. the octahedron-based curve advertised in Figure fig:Weightex2 as a weighted 3-design curve on S^3 averages omega_1^2 to 1/3 != 1/4. (The identity is correct for d = 2, and for t <= 1 only constants and odd/linear moments are involved, so those cases stand.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the construction but replace the linear height sweep: on each [Lambda_{i-1}, Lambda_i] choose w_R (odd-reflected) to push Lebesgue measure forward to lambda(x_i) mu_d(s) ds with mu_d(s) = (omega_{d-1}/omega_d)(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}, e.g. via the CDF of mu_d. Then the fiber-averaging identity and the final disintegration hold in every dimension; since each segment still travels pole-to-pole, the length bounds (>= pi|X|, equality for constant M), the singularity set {Lambda_i}, and all asymptotic conclusions of thm:weight and thm:weightstrength are preserved verbatim (for d=2 this reduces to the original formula).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:weightconst is false for d >= 3, t >= 2. The general-dimension proof of Theorem thm:weight therefore establishes nothing for d >= 4, Theorem thm:weightstrength is unproved for curves on S^d with d >= 3, and the abstract/intro claims of asymptotically optimal weighted t-design curves on all S^d are unestablished. The explicit d=2 family, the d=3 lift family via thm:S3stitch, and Proposition pro:weightEG are unaffected.
issues.title: Disintegration step in Theorem thm:weightconst is valid only for d=2; construction fails on S^d for d>=3, t>=2
issues.why_classification: The defect invalidates the paper's central weighted-setting construction in all dimensions d >= 3 and with it the proofs of both dependent theorems, but a contained modification of the sweep parametrization repairs the argument while preserving every stated conclusion, rate, and advertised regime; no new global proof architecture or loss of content results.

issues.failure_explanation: Both theorems quantify over n in N = {0,1,...}. diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then take $W_Y$ to be double the sum of all weights of edges of $\mathcal T_Y$

issues.failure_explanation: The bound fails on two counts. (i) Constant/direction: a minimal-spanning-tree edge can be as long as twice the covering radius (its midpoint lies within rho_t of each endpoint), so the valid general bound is W_t <= 4(|Y_t|-1) rho_t (recall W_t is double the tree weight) — the claimed (|Y_t|-1) rho_t/4 is a factor 16 too strong. (ii) Notion: the cited asymptotic input, pro:covrad as stated, controls D_t, the maximal nearest-neighbor distance of Y_t, not the covering radius, and tree edges are not bounded by any nearest-neighbor distance (two dense, well-separated clusters have small nearest-neighbor distances but force a long inter-cluster tree edge). Thus the step deriving W_t \lesssim t^{2n-1} from rho_t \asymp 1/t rests on an inequality that is false as written and on a proposition that, as stated, does not control the quantity used.

failure_location.quote: Noting from the definition of $W_t$ in Subsection \ref{sub:connecting} and considering the covering radius $\rho_t$ of $Y_t$, we can see that $W_t\leq (|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4$.

issues.overall_effect: The estimates W_t \lesssim t^{2n-1}, and with them the two-sided length asymptotic ell(gamma_t) \asymp t^{2n} in thm:main and the length order inherited by thm:even, rest on a defective inequality; all of these conclusions remain recoverable with the standard correct inputs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: guaranteed to exist from the theorem paired with Remark \ref{rmk:changec} for $\varepsilon_t:=W_t/(\pi|Y_t|)$

issues.failure_explanation: Since epsilon_t = W_t/(pi |Y_t|) with |Y_t| \asymp t^{2n}, the proved upper bound W_t \lesssim t^{2n-1} yields only epsilon_t \lesssim 1/t; the final sentence asserts a two-sided asymptotic without any lower bound on W_t. Such a lower bound requires every spanning-tree edge to have length \gtrsim 1/t, i.e. a separation estimate sigma_t = min_{y1 != y2} d(y1,y2) \gtrsim 1/t for the complex projective t-designs Y_t (giving W_t >= 2(|Y_t|-1) sigma_t \asymp t^{2n-1}). No separation lower bound is stated, cited, or proved anywhere in the source; pro:covrad bounds only the maximal nearest-neighbor distance, which gives no per-edge lower bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Observing that $\Pi(G_y)=e_y([0,1])$, we can see that $\Pi(\Gamma_Y)$ is exactly the union of the edges and vertices of the connected graph $\mathcal T_Y$ and thus is connected.

issues.failure_explanation: The two displayed conclusions require a simple closed curve gamma_Y whose image is all of Gamma_Y (they total the full sets union of G_y and union of D_y). But Gamma_Y is a 2-regular network — at every junction exactly one circle arc meets one geodesic — hence a priori a disjoint union of simple closed curves. The proof only observes that the projection Pi(Gamma_Y) = T_Y is connected, which does not imply Gamma_Y is connected: circle remnants over different fibers could close into separate loops over the same connected tree. The existence of the required gamma_Y is therefore not established. The conclusion is true (Gamma_Y is the boundary of a ribbon thickening of the contractible graph T_Y, hence of a disk, whose boundary is one circle), but this or an equivalent inductive argument is missing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the triple of the set $\{(0,0,-1)\}$, the curve $s\mapsto(2\sqrt{2}\cos s,2\sqrt{2}\sin s,1)/3$, and the balancing constant $1/4$ constitutes a hybrid 2-design

issues.failure_explanation: Write S = sum_X f, G = int_gamma f, I = int_{S^d cap P} f ds, L = length of the circle S^d cap P, ell = ell(gamma); since s > t, sum_{X_P} f = (s/L) I for f in P_t. Equating the two hybrid functionals on P_t gives three scalar conditions rho/|X| = rho'/(|X|+s), (1-rho)/ell = (1-rho')/(ell - L), and rho' s/((|X|+s) L) = (1-rho')/(ell - L). This overdetermined system forces the unique values rho = |X| L/(|X| L + s ell) and rho' = rho (1 + s/|X|) — not rho + 2 pi/ell(gamma). So the stated equivalence is false in general: e.g. starting from the tetrahedron as a 2-design set on S^2 (|X| = 1, s = 3, ell = L = 4 sqrt(2) pi/3), the remark's formula yields the balancing constant 1 - 3/(2 sqrt(2)) < 0 for Ehler's hybrid 2-design, whose correct constant (quoted in the same paragraph) is 1/4 = |X|/(|X|+s); applied forward to that example it gives 1/4 + 3/(2 sqrt(2)) > 1, outside the allowed range [0,1] of balancing constants.
